description: Analyse multiple domains in parallel and compare their GEO scores side by side. Returns a comparison table with overall scores, per-category breakdowns, and a ranked summary. Useful for competitive analysis or auditing a portfolio of sites. Accepts up to 50 domains per call - for larger lists, split them across multiple runs and merge the results. Before analysing, decide what kind of page this is (look at it or call extract_page_content, which returns the detected type and the text) and pass page_type; without it, checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. Here the page is the site's homepage: pass "homepage" unless the front page is itself another kind of page (a news front or blog index is "index", a one-page local business site is "service", a single-product site is "product"). Use output_format='json' to get raw results that can be passed to export_bulk_report.

domains.description: List of 2-50 domains to compare, e.g. ["example.com", "competitor.com"]. Do not include https:// prefix. For more than 50 domains, run multiple times and combine the output.

max_pages.description: Maximum pages to crawl per domain (1 = homepage only). Defaults to 10.

output_format.description: Output format. "text" (default) returns a human-readable comparison table. "json" returns the raw analysis results that can be passed to export_bulk_report.

page_type.description: What kind of page it is, as you judged it. One of: homepage (The front page of a site or brand: what it offers and where to go next); product (One product for sale, with its price, options and details); category (A shop listing of several products, often with filters and sorting); article (A news story, blog post, guide or essay); index (A news front, blog index or hub page that lists and links to other pages); docs (Technical documentation, a reference page or a dictionary entry); faq (Questions and answers, or a help-centre article about a product or service); service (A business selling a service: trades, practices, restaurants, agencies or software); lodging (A hotel, B&B, campsite or holiday rental with rooms to book); event (One event, concert or show with its date, venue and tickets); recipe (A recipe with ingredients and steps); info (Information from a government body or a nonprofit organisation); contact (Contact details, an about page, terms, privacy or an imprint); forum (A discussion thread, or a question with answers from users). Without it (or with "auto"), checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. An unknown value is ignored with a note. One id applies to every domain's homepage. A map of domain or URL -> id sets each one, e.g. {"a.com": "homepage", "b.com": "service"}; a domain it does not name runs unconfirmed.

render_mode.description: How to fetch HTML for each domain. "static" (default), "auto" (static with Chrome fallback on bot-block), or "chrome" (always render via local headless Chrome).

name: compare_domains
